Bell-to-bell phone ban made official for all Pennsylvania schools

Gov. Josh Shapiro has officially banned all personal mobile devices in Pennsylvania schools, joining 26 other states in adopting a bell-to-bell restriction statewide.

The law comes amid growing concern over young people’s mental health, as rates of anxiety, depression and even suicide are on the rise, even among elementary-age children. Continue reading…

A night with Philly’s ghost hunters at Fort Mifflin

What would a night at one of Philly’s reportedly most haunted spots be like? BP reporter Davis Cuffe joined 50 paranormal enthusiasts to find out. They went on an overnight investigation at Fort Mifflin, where ghost hunting takes patience, expensive equipment and an open mind. Continue reading…

RECAP: What else happened?

$ = paywalled

• President Trump’s Department of Justice plans to send federal election monitors to observe polling places in Allegheny, Lehigh, Luzerne and Philadelphia counties next Tuesday, Nov. 3/Election Day. [Capital-Star]

• Pennsylvania’s Act 1 guarantees help for formerly incarcerated students. Some say it’s falling short. [Chalkbeat]

• Torn testimony, boos and public shaming: Inside the contentious hearing on the Academy of Natural Sciences, where city legislators questioned whether Drexel was making a ‘land grab’ in its abrupt closure of the museum. [PhillyVoice]

• Eighth District civic “one-stop shop” helps voters cast ballots with confidence. [Germantown Info Hub]

• Philadelphia Housing Authority set to bring 63 affordable homes to Sharswood via a new senior development. [WHYY] 

• Paws for applause: Pets stepped out in costume for the annual Chestnut Hill Halloween Pet Costume Parade. [Billy Penn]

MAYOR WATCH

Mayor Parker participates in a closed-door panel hosted by Axios on Greater Philadelphia economic development and growth. (9:45 a.m.) 

She then attends a city unveiling of “Flip the Script” Resource Guide designed to support people reentering their communities with essential services and resources. (11 a.m.) 

Parker later attends the Battle of the High School Bands as part of the One Philly HBCU Week Showcase. (6 p.m.)
